title: Thesis to publication content plan
text: This plan guides editorial restructuring only. It does not change the completed thesis, data, models, or reported results.

title: Thesis to publication content plan
text:
Editorial guardrails

Preserve citation keys unless a verified bibliographic correction is needed.
Distinguish editorial revision from analytical revision in commit messages and the publication change log.
Do not alter raw data or thesis-era generated objects.
Do not present a new result until its publication-specific analysis and supporting figure or table have been reviewed.

title: Publication manuscript development
text:
This standalone Quarto project is the publication-development workspace for the Redwood Multiaged Experiment. It is intentionally separate from the legacy profile-driven project in analysis/.
The manuscript will retain the thesis as its substantive starting point while being reorganized around a regeneration-first pyro-silviculture narrative. Fuel conditions will be reported as disaggregated reference values that can support future fire-modeling work.

title: Publication manuscript development
text:
Working boundaries
This project does not execute or alter the thesis-era analyses. Future publication-specific derived data, model objects, figures, and tables will be written to ../analysis/outputs/publication/. Shared raw data, utilities, figures, and bibliography resources remain in their established repository locations until a stable shared interface is deliberately extracted.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text: Draft after the main-text results, figures, and supplementary material are defined. The abstract should state the study setting, retained-overstory design, regeneration findings, and the role of fuel measurements as reference conditions without overstating treatment comparisons.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Regeneration under varying overstory retention
Present regeneration outcomes first. The thesis results provide the starting material for basal area, Douglas-fir occurrence, and sprout-height summaries; their final wording, figures, and any revised summaries remain subject to modeling review.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Fuel conditions as reference values
Present fuel conditions second. Separate fuel components where the new publication analysis supports that distinction. Emphasize measurements that are useful as reference values for future fire modeling, while retaining comparison with prior studies only where it improves interpretation.
